grapes.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
grapes.fun_fact: A natural cross of Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc discovered in the 17th century.

grapes.name: Merlot
grapes.fun_fact: Named after the blackbird (merle) that loves eating the ripe grapes.

grapes.name: Pinot Noir
grapes.fun_fact: One of the oldest cultivated grapes, possibly grown by Romans in Burgundy.

grapes.name: Syrah
grapes.fun_fact: DNA testing showed Syrah originated in southeastern France, not Persia.

grapes.name: Tempranillo
grapes.fun_fact: Name comes from 'temprano' meaning 'early' — it ripens earlier than most Spanish reds.

grapes.name: Sangiovese
grapes.fun_fact: Italy's most planted red grape, meaning 'blood of Jove'.

grapes.name: Nebbiolo
grapes.fun_fact: Named from 'nebbia' (fog), for the autumn fogs of Piedmont during harvest.

grapes.name: Grenache
grapes.fun_fact: Produces some of the most alcoholic dry wines — up to 16% naturally.

grapes.name: Mourvèdre
grapes.fun_fact: Needs extreme heat and sunshine — thrives in Bandol's sun-drenched terroir.

grapes.name: Malbec
grapes.fun_fact: Almost extinct from French vineyards after the 1956 frost, but thrived in Argentina.

grapes.name: Cabernet Franc
grapes.fun_fact: One of the parents of Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, and Carménère.

grapes.name: Zinfandel
grapes.fun_fact: DNA proved it's the same as Croatia's Tribidrag, one of the oldest cultivated grapes.

grapes.name: Petit Verdot
grapes.fun_fact: Name means 'little green one' — it ripens very late and often incompletely in Bordeaux.

grapes.name: Gamay
grapes.fun_fact: Famously banned from Burgundy by Philip the Bold in 1395 as a 'vile and disloyal' grape.

grapes.name: Barbera
grapes.fun_fact: Most planted red grape in Piedmont — even more than Nebbiolo.

grapes.name: Carménère
grapes.fun_fact: Thought extinct until 1994 when Chilean vineyards realized their 'Merlot' was Carménère.

grapes.name: Tannat
grapes.fun_fact: Has the highest concentration of procyanidins of any wine grape, linked to longevity.

grapes.name: Touriga Nacional
grapes.fun_fact: Considered Portugal's noblest grape, backbone of both Port and top Douro reds.

grapes.name: Pinotage
grapes.fun_fact: Created in 1925 by crossing Pinot Noir and Cinsault (called Hermitage in SA).

grapes.name: Dolcetto
grapes.fun_fact: Despite meaning 'little sweet one', it makes dry wines — the name refers to the grape's sweetness.

grapes.name: Aglianico
grapes.fun_fact: Called the 'Barolo of the South' — one of Italy's most age-worthy grapes.

grapes.name: Corvina
grapes.fun_fact: Key grape in Amarone — dried on straw mats (appassimento) to concentrate sugars.

grapes.name: Nero d'Avola
grapes.fun_fact: Sicily's most important red grape, sometimes called 'the Syrah of Sicily'.

grapes.name: Chardonnay
grapes.fun_fact: The world's most popular white wine grape — grown on every wine-producing continent.

grapes.name: Sauvignon Blanc
grapes.fun_fact: One of the parents of Cabernet Sauvignon (crossed with Cabernet Franc).

grapes.name: Riesling
grapes.fun_fact: One of few whites that can age for decades — great Rieslings improve for 30+ years.

grapes.name: Pinot Grigio
grapes.fun_fact: The grey-pink skin can make richly colored 'orange wines' with extended skin contact.

grapes.name: Gewürztraminer
grapes.fun_fact: Gewürz means 'spice' in German — one of the most aromatic grapes in existence.

grapes.name: Sémillon
grapes.fun_fact: The key grape of Sauternes — its thin skin is perfectly suited to noble rot (botrytis).

grapes.name: Chenin Blanc
grapes.fun_fact: Incredibly versatile — makes dry, sweet, sparkling, and everything in between.

grapes.name: Viognier
grapes.fun_fact: Nearly went extinct in the 1960s — only 8 hectares remained in Condrieu.

grapes.name: Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains
grapes.fun_fact: Possibly the oldest domesticated grape — may be the ancestor of all vinifera varieties.

grapes.name: Albariño
grapes.fun_fact: Thick skins protect it from the wet maritime climate of Galicia.

grapes.name: Grüner Veltliner
grapes.fun_fact: Austria's signature grape — at a famous 2002 tasting, it beat top Burgundy blind.

grapes.name: Torrontés
grapes.fun_fact: A natural cross of Muscat and Criolla — Argentina's signature white grape.

grapes.name: Verdejo
grapes.fun_fact: Nearly destroyed by phylloxera, then neglected until Marqués de Riscal revived it in the 1970s.

grapes.name: Vermentino
grapes.fun_fact: Thrives in coastal Mediterranean heat — one of the best whites for hot climates.

grapes.name: Marsanne
grapes.fun_fact: Named after the village of Marsanne near Montélimar in the northern Rhône.

grapes.name: Roussanne
grapes.fun_fact: Named for its russet (roux) colored skin when ripe.

grapes.name: Trebbiano
grapes.fun_fact: The world's most planted white grape by area — mostly distilled into Cognac and brandy.

grapes.name: Pinot Blanc
grapes.fun_fact: A mutation of Pinot Noir — genetically identical except for skin color.

grapes.name: Muscadet
grapes.fun_fact: Survived the 1709 frost that killed most Loire vines — prized for cold hardiness.

grapes.name: Garganega
grapes.fun_fact: The backbone of Soave — capable of making complex age-worthy wines in the right hands.

grapes.name: Fiano
grapes.fun_fact: Loved by bees — Latin name 'Vitis apiana' from 'apis' (bee).

grapes.name: Greco
grapes.fun_fact: Believed to have been brought to southern Italy by ancient Greek colonists.

grapes.name: Godello
grapes.fun_fact: Nearly extinct by the 1970s, revived by a handful of passionate winemakers in Valdeorras.

grapes.name: Assyrtiko
grapes.fun_fact: Grown ungrafted on phylloxera-free Santorini, some vines are over 200 years old.

grapes.name: Cinsault
grapes.fun_fact: One of the parents of Pinotage (crossed with Pinot Noir in South Africa).

grapes.name: Carignan
grapes.fun_fact: Old-vine Carignan (80-100+ years) produces some of the greatest wines of southern France.

grapes.name: Counoise
grapes.fun_fact: One of the 13 permitted grapes of Châteauneuf-du-Pape.

grapes.name: Vaccarèse
grapes.fun_fact: One of the rarest of the 13 Châteauneuf-du-Pape grapes.

grapes.name: Muscardin
grapes.fun_fact: Named for its musky aroma — barely planted even in Châteauneuf.

grapes.name: Terret Noir
grapes.fun_fact: Another rare Châteauneuf grape — mostly found in field blends.

grapes.name: Picpoul Noir
grapes.fun_fact: Red sibling of the popular white Picpoul — 'lip stinger' for its high acidity.

grapes.name: Piquepoul Blanc
grapes.fun_fact: The 'Muscadet of the South' — the perfect oyster wine from the Mediterranean.

grapes.name: Clairette Blanche
grapes.fun_fact: One of the white grapes of Châteauneuf-du-Pape — also makes sparkling Clairette de Die.

grapes.name: Bourboulenc
grapes.fun_fact: Late ripening white grape valued for maintaining acidity in hot southern blends.

grapes.name: Grenache Blanc
grapes.fun_fact: White mutation of Grenache Noir — makes rich, full whites in the southern Rhône.

grapes.name: Nerello Mascalese
grapes.fun_fact: Called 'the Pinot Noir of the Mediterranean' for its elegance on Etna's volcanic slopes.

grapes.name: Montepulciano
grapes.fun_fact: Not related to the town of Montepulciano in Tuscany — that uses Sangiovese (Prugnolo).

grapes.name: Primitivo
grapes.fun_fact: Identical to Zinfandel — brought to Puglia from Croatia centuries ago.

grapes.name: Negroamaro
grapes.fun_fact: Name literally means 'black bitter' — a double redundancy since negro and amaro both mean dark.

grapes.name: Lagrein
grapes.fun_fact: Genetically related to Syrah — DNA shows they share a parent grape (Teroldego?).

grapes.name: Schiava
grapes.fun_fact: Name means 'slave girl' — once trained on pergola trellises like captives on a leash.

grapes.name: Teroldego
grapes.fun_fact: Possibly a parent of both Lagrein and Syrah — a key link in ampelographic genetics.

grapes.name: Frappato
grapes.fun_fact: The 'Gamay of Sicily' — makes joyfully light, aromatic reds.

grapes.name: Canaiolo
grapes.fun_fact: Traditional blending partner for Sangiovese in old-style Chianti recipes.

grapes.name: Sagrantino
grapes.fun_fact: Has more tannin than any other grape — originally made as a sweet passito wine.

grapes.name: Verdicchio
grapes.fun_fact: Italy's greatest native white? Age-worthy and mineral — often compared to Chablis.

grapes.name: Falanghina
grapes.fun_fact: Possibly the grape behind ancient Falernian wine — Rome's most prized vintage.

grapes.name: Arneis
grapes.fun_fact: Name means 'little rascal' in Piedmontese — difficult to grow and vinify.

grapes.name: Garnacha Tintorera
grapes.fun_fact: One of the few teinturier grapes — red flesh as well as red skin.

grapes.name: Graciano
grapes.fun_fact: Provides backbone and color to Rioja blends — prized but low-yielding.

grapes.name: Mencía
grapes.fun_fact: Spain's 'answer to Pinot Noir' — elegant and terroir-driven from slate soils of Bierzo.

grapes.name: Garnacha Blanca
grapes.fun_fact: White mutation of red Garnacha — makes rich, full-bodied Mediterranean whites.

grapes.name: Macabeo
grapes.fun_fact: The most planted white grape in Spain — key component of Cava sparkling wine.

grapes.name: Xarel·lo
grapes.fun_fact: Gives Cava its body and earthiness — increasingly bottled as still single-varietal wine.

grapes.name: Parellada
grapes.fun_fact: Grown at the highest altitudes in Penedès — provides floral delicacy to Cava.

grapes.name: Bobal
grapes.fun_fact: Spain's third most planted red grape — gaining recognition for quality after decades of bulk wine.

grapes.name: Listán Negro
grapes.fun_fact: Grown ungrafted on phylloxera-free volcanic soils of the Canary Islands.

grapes.name: Touriga Franca
grapes.fun_fact: The most planted grape in the Douro — provides aromatic complexity to Port blends.

grapes.name: Tinta Barroca
grapes.fun_fact: Ripens earlier than other Douro grapes — planted on cooler north-facing slopes.

grapes.name: Tinta Cão
grapes.fun_fact: Once nearly extinct — prized for elegance and acidity in Port blends.

grapes.name: Baga
grapes.fun_fact: Portugal's most tannic grape — great Bairrada Baga ages like top Barolo.

grapes.name: Castelão
grapes.fun_fact: Portugal's most planted red grape — known as Periquita after a famous wine brand.

grapes.name: Trincadeira
grapes.fun_fact: Thrives in the blazing heat of Portugal's Alentejo plains.

grapes.name: Alvarinho
grapes.fun_fact: Same grape as Spain's Albariño — makes Portugal's finest Vinho Verde.

grapes.name: Loureiro
grapes.fun_fact: Named after laurel (loureiro means laurel tree) — intensely floral and aromatic.

grapes.name: Arinto
grapes.fun_fact: Portugal's finest white grape for acidity — maintains freshness even in hot Alentejo.

grapes.name: Encruzado
grapes.fun_fact: Portugal's noblest white — compared to white Burgundy for its aging ability and complexity.

grapes.name: Fernão Pires
grapes.fun_fact: Portugal's most planted white grape — aromatic and versatile.

grapes.name: Palomino Fino
grapes.fun_fact: Makes unremarkable table wine but extraordinary Sherry — flor yeast transforms it.

grapes.name: Pedro Ximénez
grapes.fun_fact: Sun-dried into raisins before pressing — makes the sweetest, most concentrated wines on earth.

grapes.name: Hondarrabi Zuri
grapes.fun_fact: The grape behind txakoli — poured from a height for a slight spritz.

grapes.name: Prieto Picudo
grapes.fun_fact: A rare León grape making a comeback — traditionally makes rosado by a unique method.

grapes.name: Müller-Thurgau
grapes.fun_fact: Created by crossing Riesling and Madeleine Royale in 1882 — not Silvaner as once thought.

grapes.name: Silvaner
grapes.fun_fact: Once Germany's most planted grape before being overtaken by Müller-Thurgau and Riesling.

grapes.name: Scheurebe
grapes.fun_fact: A Riesling × Silvaner cross — produces extraordinary Beerenauslese and TBA wines.

grapes.name: Kerner
grapes.fun_fact: A Trollinger (Schiava) × Riesling cross — named after poet Justinus Kerner.

grapes.name: Bacchus
grapes.fun_fact: A cross of Silvaner × Riesling and Müller-Thurgau — increasingly popular in England.

grapes.name: Dornfelder
grapes.fun_fact: Germany's most popular red grape — created in 1955, deeper in color than Pinot Noir.

grapes.name: Portugieser
grapes.fun_fact: Despite the name, not from Portugal — probably originated in Austria or Hungary.

grapes.name: Lemberger
grapes.fun_fact: Austria's noblest red grape — Blaufränkisch from Burgenland rivals top Pinot Noir.

grapes.name: Zweigelt
grapes.fun_fact: Austria's most planted red — a 1922 cross of Blaufränkisch and St. Laurent.

grapes.name: St. Laurent
grapes.fun_fact: A spontaneous Pinot Noir cross — tastes like a wilder, spicier Pinot.

grapes.name: Welschriesling
grapes.fun_fact: No relation to true Riesling — 'Welsch' means foreign/Romance in German.

grapes.name: Rotgipfler
grapes.fun_fact: Nearly extinct — only grown in a tiny area south of Vienna with its partner Zierfandler.

grapes.name: Zierfandler
grapes.fun_fact: Traditional partner of Rotgipfler — together they make the classic Gumpoldskirchner blend.

grapes.name: Furmint
grapes.fun_fact: Makes Tokaji Aszú — the original 'wine of kings, king of wines' since the 1600s.

grapes.name: Hárslevelű
grapes.fun_fact: Name means 'linden leaf' — intensely aromatic, perfect partner for Furmint in Tokaji.

grapes.name: Kadarka
grapes.fun_fact: Once the dominant grape of Bull's Blood (Egri Bikavér) — now a rare specialty.

grapes.name: Juhfark
grapes.fun_fact: Grown on volcanic Somló hill — tradition says drinking it on wedding night ensures male heirs.

grapes.name: Xinomavro
grapes.fun_fact: Called the 'Nebbiolo of Greece' — high acid, high tannin, pale color, incredible aging.

grapes.name: Agiorgitiko
grapes.fun_fact: Greece's most planted red — makes everything from rosé to deep reds in Nemea.

grapes.name: Moschofilero
grapes.fun_fact: A pink-skinned grape that makes aromatic white wine — sometimes compared to Gewürztraminer.

grapes.name: Malagousia
grapes.fun_fact: Rescued from extinction in the 1970s by winemaker Evangelos Gerovassiliou.

grapes.name: Vidiano
grapes.fun_fact: A rare Cretan grape recently revived — producing lush, full-bodied whites.

grapes.name: Mavrodaphne
grapes.fun_fact: Greece's answer to Port — sweet, fortified, and named 'black laurel'.

grapes.name: Saperavi
grapes.fun_fact: A teinturier grape — red flesh and juice. Georgia's finest red, aged in qvevri for 8000 years.

grapes.name: Rkatsiteli
grapes.fun_fact: One of the world's oldest and most planted grapes — heart of Georgian amber/orange wine tradition.

grapes.name: Mtsvane
grapes.fun_fact: Mtsvane means 'green' in Georgian — softer and more aromatic than Rkatsiteli.

grapes.name: Kisi
grapes.fun_fact: Nearly extinct until recently — now a star of the Georgian qvevri wine revival.

grapes.name: Aleksandrouli
grapes.fun_fact: Makes Khvanchkara, a naturally semi-sweet red — reportedly Stalin's favorite wine.

grapes.name: Plavac Mali
grapes.fun_fact: A cross of Zinfandel/Tribidrag and Dobričić — Croatia's most prestigious red.

grapes.name: Graševina
grapes.fun_fact: Croatia's most planted grape — makes fresh, mineral whites in continental Slavonia.

grapes.name: Malvazija Istarska
grapes.fun_fact: Heart of Istria's thriving natural wine scene — superb with white truffles.

grapes.name: Fetească Neagră
grapes.fun_fact: Romania's noblest red — 'Black Maiden' produces powerful, complex wines.

grapes.name: Fetească Albă
grapes.fun_fact: One of Romania's trio of indigenous Fetească grapes.

grapes.name: Fetească Regală
grapes.fun_fact: A natural cross of Fetească Albă and Grasă de Cotnari — Romania's most planted white.

grapes.name: Tămâioasă Românească
grapes.fun_fact: Means 'frankincense grape' — incredibly aromatic, used for Romania's legendary Cotnari sweet wines.

grapes.name: Mavrud
grapes.fun_fact: Bulgaria's most prized indigenous red — legend says it was the grape of the Thracians.

grapes.name: Melnik
grapes.fun_fact: Named after the town of Melnik — Winston Churchill was said to order it by the barrel.

grapes.name: Vranec
grapes.fun_fact: Name means 'black stallion' — the powerhouse red of the western Balkans.

grapes.name: Plavina
grapes.fun_fact: A light Dalmatian red often blended or made into rosé.

grapes.name: Babić
grapes.fun_fact: Grows on dramatic terraced vineyards near Primošten — a UNESCO heritage landscape.

grapes.name: Prokupac
grapes.fun_fact: Serbia's signature indigenous red — being revived after decades of communist bulk wine.

grapes.name: Refosco dal Peduncolo Rosso
grapes.fun_fact: An ancient Friulian variety — likely ancestor of many northeastern Italian reds.

grapes.name: Ribolla Gialla
grapes.fun_fact: The poster grape of Italy's orange wine movement — Josko Gravner made it famous worldwide.

grapes.name: Schioppettino
grapes.fun_fact: Nearly went extinct — saved by a group of Friulian winemakers in the 1970s.

grapes.name: Pignolo
grapes.fun_fact: Produces only tiny pine cone-shaped clusters (pignolo = little pine cone).

grapes.name: Savagnin
grapes.fun_fact: Makes vin jaune under a layer of flor yeast — aged 6+ years, France's answer to Sherry.

grapes.name: Petite Sirah
grapes.fun_fact: A cross of Syrah and Peloursin — found its true home in California, not France.

grapes.name: Norton
grapes.fun_fact: America's only true Vitis aestivalis grape — naturally phylloxera resistant.

grapes.name: Chambourcin
grapes.fun_fact: A French-American hybrid — makes surprisingly serious reds in the eastern United States.

grapes.name: Vidal Blanc
grapes.fun_fact: Canada's ice wine star — thick skin survives extreme cold to make legendary frozen wines.

grapes.name: Seyval Blanc
grapes.fun_fact: A French hybrid that thrives in England — used in some of England's best sparkling wines.

grapes.name: Marquette
grapes.fun_fact: Survives -35°F — a University of Minnesota hybrid making serious cold-climate reds.

grapes.name: País
grapes.fun_fact: Brought by conquistadors — Chile's oldest grape, now championed by natural wine makers.

grapes.name: Criolla Grande
grapes.fun_fact: Argentina's most planted grape by area — mostly used for bulk wine and table grapes.

grapes.name: Bonarda
grapes.fun_fact: Argentina's second most planted red — confusingly, a different grape than Italian Bonarda.

grapes.name: Colombard
grapes.fun_fact: Originally for distillation into Armagnac — now makes crisp, affordable IGP wines.

grapes.name: Gros Manseng
grapes.fun_fact: Makes both dry and sweet wines — the sweet Jurançon was used to baptize Henri IV.

grapes.name: Petit Manseng
grapes.fun_fact: Tiny berries (petit) concentrate sugar naturally on the vine — no botrytis needed.

grapes.name: Négrette
grapes.fun_fact: Almost exclusive to the Fronton appellation near Toulouse — intensely aromatic and floral.

grapes.name: Trousseau
grapes.fun_fact: The red counterpart to Savagnin in the Jura — also known as Bastardo in Portugal.

grapes.name: Poulsard
grapes.fun_fact: Makes some of the palest red wines in France — so light they're often mistaken for rosé.

grapes.name: Tibouren
grapes.fun_fact: Makes some of Provence's most elegant rosés — extremely rare outside the region.

grapes.name: Petit Courbu
grapes.fun_fact: A rare Jurançon blending grape — adds complexity and elegance.

grapes.name: Len de l'El
grapes.fun_fact: Name means 'far from the eye' — the bunch hangs far from the shoot's bud.

grapes.name: Mauzac
grapes.fun_fact: The original sparkling wine grape of Limoux — sparkling Blanquette predates Champagne.

grapes.name: Jacquère
grapes.fun_fact: The mountain white of the French Alps — crisp, mineral, perfect with fondue and raclette.

grapes.name: Altesse
grapes.fun_fact: Legend says it was brought from Cyprus by a Crusader — 'Altesse' means 'highness'.

grapes.name: Obaideh
grapes.fun_fact: An ancient Lebanese grape — possibly an ancestor of Chardonnay brought by Crusaders.

grapes.name: Merwah
grapes.fun_fact: An ancient Levantine grape — possibly related to Sémillon. Rescued from near extinction.

grapes.name: Koshu
grapes.fun_fact: Arrived in Japan via the Silk Road ~1000 years ago — a pink-skinned vinifera variety.

grapes.name: Muscat Bailey A
grapes.fun_fact: Japan's most planted red hybrid — created by Zenbei Kawakami in 1927.

grapes.name: Tannat Uruguayo
grapes.fun_fact: Uruguay's national grape — adapted to produce softer tannins than French Tannat.

grapes.name: Susumaniello
grapes.fun_fact: Name means 'little donkey' — once loaded with fruit when young, production drops with age.

grapes.name: Nerello Cappuccio
grapes.fun_fact: The 'Merlot' to Nerello Mascalese's 'Cabernet' — adds softness to Etna blends.

grapes.name: Grillo
grapes.fun_fact: A key grape of Marsala — now making excellent dry table wines and stealing the spotlight.

grapes.name: Carricante
grapes.fun_fact: Mount Etna's white star — volcanic terroir gives it incredible minerality and aging potential.

grapes.name: Pecorino
grapes.fun_fact: Named for sheep (pecora) that loved eating the grapes — rescued from near-extinction in the 1990s.

grapes.name: Coda di Volpe
grapes.fun_fact: Name means 'foxtail' — for the shape of the grape cluster. Ancient Campanian variety.

grapes.name: Piedirosso
grapes.fun_fact: Name means 'red foot' — the stems turn red like a pigeon's foot (Per'e Palummo).

grapes.name: Ciliegiolo
grapes.fun_fact: Name means 'little cherry' — possibly a parent of Sangiovese.

grapes.name: Colorino
grapes.fun_fact: Used to add deep color to Chianti blends — name literally means 'the coloring one'.

grapes.name: Ruché
grapes.fun_fact: One of Piedmont's most aromatic reds — uniquely floral, only grown around one village.

grapes.name: Freisa
grapes.fun_fact: Once made as a lightly fizzy sweet red — now increasingly as a dry, serious wine.

grapes.name: Pelaverga
grapes.fun_fact: Grown almost exclusively in Verduno (Barolo zone) — intensely peppery and aromatic.

grapes.name: Nascetta
grapes.fun_fact: A rediscovered Langhe white — potentially Piedmont's great native white grape.

grapes.name: Tintilia
grapes.fun_fact: Molise's only native grape of significance — rescued from extinction in the 2000s.

grapes.name: Gaglioppo
grapes.fun_fact: Calabria's noble grape — Cirò was allegedly the wine given to Olympic victors in ancient Greece.

grapes.name: Schiava Grossa
grapes.fun_fact: Also popular as a table grape (Black Hamburg) — Württemberg drinks more of it than anywhere.

grapes.name: Pinot Meunier
grapes.fun_fact: The 'workhorse' of Champagne — provides fruity roundness and buds later to avoid frost.

grapes.name: Muscat of Alexandria
grapes.fun_fact: One of the oldest grape varieties — possibly cultivated by Pharaohs in ancient Egypt.

grapes.name: Malvasia
grapes.fun_fact: A whole family of grapes — not one variety but many, all sharing the Malvasia name.

grapes.name: Chasselas
grapes.fun_fact: Switzerland's most planted grape — uniquely transparent, reflecting terroir more than fruit.

grapes.name: Completer
grapes.fun_fact: One of Switzerland's rarest grapes — traditionally served as the 'completing' wine after a meal.

grapes.name: Cornalin
grapes.fun_fact: A parent of Syrah — only grown in Switzerland's sunny Valais. Nearly went extinct.

grapes.name: Petite Arvine
grapes.fun_fact: Switzerland's most distinctive native white — uniquely salty finish, unlike any other grape.

grapes.name: Amigne
grapes.fun_fact: Grown almost exclusively in Vétroz — bottles marked with 1-3 bees indicating sweetness level.

grapes.name: Verdelho
grapes.fun_fact: One of the noble Madeira grapes — makes medium-dry style, between Sercial and Bual.

grapes.name: Sercial
grapes.fun_fact: Makes the driest style of Madeira — 'Esgana Cão' means 'dog strangler' for its acidity.

grapes.name: Bual
grapes.fun_fact: Makes medium-sweet Madeira — rich and complex, prized by Thomas Jefferson.

grapes.name: Malmsey
grapes.fun_fact: The sweetest, richest style of Madeira — Duke of Clarence reportedly drowned in a butt of it.

grapes.name: Tinta Negra
grapes.fun_fact: Makes ~85% of all Madeira — versatile enough to imitate all four noble grape styles.

grapes.name: Sousão
grapes.fun_fact: Incredibly deep color — used in Port blends and also makes intense Vinho Verde reds.

grapes.name: Auxerrois
grapes.fun_fact: Often blended with Pinot Blanc and sold as such — genetically distinct but very similar.

grapes.name: Muscadelle
grapes.fun_fact: The third grape of Sauternes — adds perfume and floral lift to the blend.

grapes.name: Mouyssaguès
grapes.fun_fact: One of the rarest French grapes — survives only in a few vineyards in Aveyron.

grapes.name: Fer Servadou
grapes.fun_fact: Name means 'hard iron' — gives wines a distinctive metallic/mineral character.
